developments: Bitcoin broke its June-July low overnight, falling from about $58,900 to as low as $55,100 on Kraken, and traded near $56,000 at 06:30 UK, its lowest since September 2024, CoinDesk reported.
About $2.4 billion of leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, more than $1 billion of it in Bitcoin futures, according to CoinGlass data cited by CoinDesk.
ZEC fell to a low of about $678 on Kraken in the 03:00 UK hour and traded near $699, down about 5% since the evening edition and about 19% over 24 hours.
briefing.changed: Last night's question was whether the summer low near $57,700 would hold over the weekend. It did not: the break came at about 03:00 UK in thin Asian trading, and forced selling widened from about $1.5 billion to about $2.4 billion.
briefing.question: Is $55,000 the point where forced selling runs out, or does the weekend bring a deeper flush before US markets reopen on Monday?
briefing.watch: Friday's US spot bitcoin ETF flow figures, still to be confirmed, and Monday's US open at 14:30 UK. The next 🔴 event is the Fed decision on Wednesday 9 December at 19:00 UK.

lead.headline: Bitcoin breaks summer low, sinks to two-year bottom near $55,000
lead.standfirst: Bitcoin fell through its June-July low in early Asian trading on Saturday, touching $55,100 on Kraken, as about $2.4 billion of leveraged crypto bets were wiped out in a day.
body: Bitcoin fell as low as $55,100 on Saturday morning, Kraken data showed, after the slide that began on Friday cut through the June-July low near $57,700. It traded near $56,000 at 06:30 UK time, about 4% below the level at Friday's evening edition.

The steepest leg came in the 03:00 UK hour, when the price dropped from about $58,500 to $56,300. CoinDesk reported that Bitcoin was at its lowest since September 2024 and down about 28% this quarter.

About $2.40 billion of crypto futures positions were liquidated over 24 hours, with more than $1 billion in Bitcoin and $545 million in Ether, according to CoinGlass data cited by CoinDesk. The largest single liquidation was a $51.7 million long Bitcoin bet.

The fall followed a broad sell-off on Wall Street on Friday. The Nasdaq Composite fell about 5% and the S&P 500 about 3.5%, Bitcoin Magazine reported, with Nvidia down about 12.5%. CoinDesk said analysts pointed to rising inflation-adjusted US Treasury yields and a more hawkish Fed outlook.

Zcash fell harder, to a low of about $678 on Kraken, and other large coins including XRP and Solana dropped about 9% in 24 hours, CoinDesk said. Thursday's US spot bitcoin ETF outflow was $582 million, The Block reported; Friday's figure had not been confirmed at publication.

headline: Bitcoin broke its summer low overnight, touching $55,100 and trading near $56,000, its lowest since September 2024, as about $2.4 billion of leveraged bets were liquidated. ZEC fell to about $699, after a low near $678.
spoken: Cryptonaire Post, morning edition, Saturday the twenty first of November. Bitcoin broke through its summer low overnight. It fell to about fifty five thousand one hundred dollars around four in the morning UK time and is now near fifty six thousand, its lowest in about two years. About two point four billion dollars of leveraged bets were wiped out in a day. The fall followed a five percent drop in the Nasdaq on Friday. Zcash is near six hundred and ninety nine dollars, after touching about six hundred and seventy eight. The next big event is the Fed decision on the ninth of December at seven in the evening. Information only, not advice.

stories.title: Bitcoin breaks its June-July low, touches $55,100
stories.why: Kraken showed Bitcoin near $58,900 at midnight UK, then a fall from about $58,500 to $56,300 in the 03:00 UK hour and a low of $55,100 in the 06:00 hour; it traded near $56,030 at 06:30 UK. CoinDesk said it was the lowest since September 2024 and a 28% quarterly decline. This changes last night's assessment: the summer low near $57,700 did not hold.

note.read: With the well-watched summer low gone, the market has no recent support level, and the break came in thin weekend Asian trading when forced selling travels further.
note.alt: Breaks in thin weekend trading often overshoot; the record liquidation total may mark forced sellers running out rather than new spot selling.
note.change: A quick recovery back above about $57,700 would suggest a false break; a further fall with liquidations staying high would suggest the slide is still being driven by leverage.

stories.title: Liquidations climb to about $2.4 billion as the Nasdaq falls 5%
stories.why: CoinGlass data cited by CoinDesk showed $2.40 billion of crypto futures liquidated over 24 hours, up from about $1.5 billion at the evening edition, with more than $1 billion in Bitcoin. Bitcoin Magazine reported the Nasdaq Composite fell about 5% and the S&P 500 about 3.5% on Friday, with Nvidia down about 12.5% and Strategy down about 8.4%. The new evidence is that the US sell-off deepened into the close and crypto kept falling after stocks shut.
stories.caveat: Bitcoin Magazine, citing Yahoo Finance, gave about $1.53 billion of liquidations at its earlier time; CoinDesk's $2.40 billion is the later, wider count.

note.read: Crypto is the only market open at the weekend, so it is absorbing selling pressure from Friday's equity rout on its own.
note.alt: Some of the overnight move may be leverage being cleared rather than fresh selling, which tends to fade once open interest has reset.
note.change: Stable US stock futures on Sunday evening and lower liquidation totals would point to the pressure easing.

stories.title: ZEC falls to about $678 low, trades near $699
stories.why: Kraken showed ZEC near $758 at midnight UK, then a fall to $677.61 in the 03:00 UK hour alongside Bitcoin's break, and about $699 at 06:30 UK. CoinDesk put ZEC's 24-hour fall at about 19%, against about 9% for Bitcoin. The Block noted ZEC is now about 55% below its all-time high of $1,680 from about two months ago. The new evidence is that ZEC fell with Bitcoin's break but did not lead it.

note.read: ZEC is still moving at about twice Bitcoin's pace in both directions, as a high-beta coin in a risk-off market.
note.alt: ZEC's small bounce off $678 while Bitcoin made a fresh low at 06:00 UK may show its extra selling is slowing.
note.change: ZEC holding above $678 if Bitcoin falls further would suggest its relative weakness is fading.

stories.title: Thursday ETF outflow $582 million, IBIT's largest on record; Friday still unconfirmed
stories.why: US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $582 million on Thursday, with BlackRock's IBIT accounting for $541.1 million, its largest one-day outflow on record, Bitcoin Magazine and The Block reported. November outflows are now about $3.5 billion. Friday's total, covering the day Bitcoin broke $60,000, had not been confirmed by a reputable source at publication.

stories.title: Zebra 7.2.0-beta.3 out; Zcash fee cut is now active
stories.why: The Zcash Foundation published the Zebra 7.2.0-beta.3 pre-release on Friday evening. Its notes say Mainnet passed the ZIP 2009 fee reduction height on 19 November, so the marginal fee is now 400 zatoshis per action. It is a beta with no network upgrade; Zebra 7.1.0's end-of-support warnings begin around 3 December.

stories.title: DCG's Zcash miner Fortitude clears shareholder vote for Nasdaq listing
stories.why: HeartSciences shareholders approved the merger with Fortitude, with about 86% in favour, The Block reported; the combined Fortitude Mining Group still needs Nasdaq approval and has no listing date. Fortitude said its Zcash hashrate rose about 15% to 5.4 GSol/s since early October. It would be a listed company tied to ZEC mining.

explained.title: Why weekend breaks can overshoot
body: Crypto trades every day, but the big buyers that usually step in, such as ETF desks and US funds, mostly work when US markets are open. At the weekend, fewer orders sit on the books, so a large sale or a wave of forced liquidations moves the price further than it would on a weekday.

That is why traders watch whether a weekend break holds once Monday's US session opens: a level reclaimed then can mean the move was mostly thin trading, while a level that stays broken suggests real selling.

investigating: How large were Friday's US spot bitcoin ETF outflows as Bitcoin broke $60,000? Evidence: SoSoValue or Farside daily totals; Farside could not be read this morning.
Has the leverage now been cleared? Evidence: Bitcoin futures open interest and funding rates on Saturday and Sunday compared with Friday.
Do Bitcoin treasury companies or miners face pressure at these prices? Evidence: filings or statements from Strategy and listed miners after JPMorgan's $86,000 production cost estimate.
